sections.content: After the adjective *határos* ("bordering"), the neighbouring country takes the *-val/-vel* ("with") ending: *Magyarország Ausztriával határos* (Hungary borders Austria, literally "is bordering with Austria"). The initial consonant of *-val/-vel* always assimilates to the consonant right before it, so it's *országgal* (not *országval*), because *ország* ends in *g*. For the compass directions (*észak*, *dél*, *kelet*, *nyugat* — north, south, east, west), you use the *-ra/-re* ("toward") and *-tól/-től* ("as seen from") endings together to say what lies where relative to something else.

sections.title: Compass directions: -ra/-re and -tól/-től
rows: north of Hungary (lit. 'to the north, from Hungary')

items.english: Slovakia is to the north of Hungary.
Austria lies to the west of Hungary.
Romania is to the east of Hungary.

sections.content: To say "X lies [direction] of Y", combine Y in *-tól/-től* with the compass word in *-ra/-re*: *Magyarországtól délre* = "south of Hungary". Don't drop the *-tól/-től* — *délre* alone just means "southward", with no reference point.
